answer: Agent economies resist sybils by making identity costly. A sudden plume of clones must each post stake and earn attestations, so none finds a trusted root to grow from. Honest agents build a vault of mutual signatures; a sybil vine of linked bots stays shallow and unverified, unable to swing any outcome. Because every fake persona pays real stake yet gains no credibility, mass impersonation becomes a losing, expensive grind rather than a free exploit.
